listing.name: TARGET: Terror (darkuni Recomp)
listing.summary: Player-managed Windows setup for the NTSC-U Wii disc.

steps.title: Prepare your Wii disc image
steps.instruction: Copy your own NTSC-U TARGET: Terror Wii disc image (RGDEA4, .iso or .ciso) into the folder beside targetterror.exe, and keep your original separately. On first start the game builds its game folder from the image, which takes a few minutes; after that the copied image is no longer needed.

steps.title: Allow space for the upstream import
steps.instruction: Run targetterror.exe and allow first-run extraction to populate game. Leave enough free space for about 4.4 GB of generated files.

steps.title: Preserve the creating profile
steps.instruction: Keep the generated game folder, targetterror.ini and nand, including high scores, with the creating runtime.

warnings: The package includes recompiled game code that the project license does not cover. Portcove downloads it only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.
Keep the upstream folder outside the Portcove library. Close the game and its helpers before backing up or replacing the creating runtime and its data.

presentation.manual_preparation: Before first Play, copy your own NTSC-U TARGET: Terror Wii disc image (RGDEA4, .iso or .ciso) into the managed folder beside targetterror.exe, and keep your original separately. On first Play the game builds its game folder from the image, which takes a few minutes and about 4.4 GB; without an image it shows Game files not found and closes. Once the game has started, delete the copied image so it is not kept in backups. The download is the recompiled player with SDL2 and contains no game data; the project license does not cover the recompiled game code, and its system font replacements are Apache-licensed Droid Sans. Core preserves game, nand (saves and high scores) and targetterror.ini across updates and backups. The log and hang report beside the game are diagnostics. The game needs a GPU with OpenGL 3.3. Portcove replaces the program; upstream owns disc import and save formats.
